title: Sample 15-6: Lines of Dialogue

illustrates.quote: 15.5.2 When a play is written in verse, observe the following guidelines: a. Use format outlined above in Formats, §15.5.1 a–c. b. Insert three blank spaces in braille when in print a significant blank space is left between the speaker’s name and the first word of the dialogue. A transcriber's note is required explaining this format.

blocks.features: Significant blank space between speaker name and dialogue (stepped verse, 15.5.2b).
Significant blank space between speaker name and dialogue (stepped verse, 15.5.2b).

blocks.text: CAESAR: Stand you directly in Antonius' way,
When he doth run his course. Antonius!
blocks.features: Continuation of Caesar's own speech, no speaker name repeated.

blocks.text: CAESAR: Forget not, in your speed, Antonius,
To touch Calpurnia; for our elders say,
The barren, touched in this holy chase,

blocks.features: Significant blank space between speaker name and dialogue (stepped verse, 15.5.2b).

blocks.text: When Caesar says 'do this,' it is perform'd.
CAESAR: Set on; and leave no ceremony out.

print.notes: Fourteen lines of verse dialogue from Julius Caesar, Act 1 Scene 2 (Shakespeare). 'level' (0 = flush with a speaker name, 1 = a continuation line of the same speech with no speaker repeated) was independently re-measured from the given, already-verified braille (leading blank cells / 2) rather than taken from either run's own say-so; both runs already agreed on every line's own wording and on the two print-visible numbers (5, 10).
print.printFeatures: Play script in verse with three 'stepped verse' lines (a shared metrical line split between two speakers, shown in print with a wide gap standing in for the first speaker's own share of the line) and right-margin line numbers every 5 lines.

braille.notes: CORRECTED during reconciliation: both A and B's own line text was byte-identical to the source's raw text extraction, but that raw extraction right-justifies each number far past column 40 (lines up to 70 characters long) even though this file's own declared braille.width is 40 and every other file in this section right-justifies its own numbers at exactly column 40 — the same text-extraction artifact found and fixed in Sample 15-2/Example 15-2 (see their own braille.notes for the full reasoning). Each line's own text and number are unchanged; only the padding was reduced so both numbered lines are exactly 40 cells (widest number '#aj'/10, 3 cells; 2-blank-cell minimum). Right-margin numbers #e=5 and #aj=10 confirmed by direct decode.

resolution: Braille: A and B agreed on every character but both preserved a raw text-extraction artifact (numbers right-justified far past the declared 40-cell width); re-justified to column 40 during this reconciliation (see braille.notes). Print side: both runs already agreed on wording, levels (by description) and the two numbers; no correction needed beyond independently re-verifying the levels against the braille. Modeled by buildModel15 as play/verse dialogue (type:'play', subtype:'verse', matching the ALREADY-established standards-map.md row for BANA 15.5.2a) with a GENUINE (not text-folded) linenum segment on the two numbered lines — per standards-map.md's own row for 15.5.2a and standards-findings.md F-181, formatPlay's segmentsToBraille call never passes lineNumbers:true on EITHER its prose or verse branch, so both numbers are expected to be silently dropped from the built output entirely (not merely misplaced): this file's mismatch cause is F-181.
